summary: Ulrich Pagel specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip T. Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme (attested 1995), and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute, later holding posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University (2008–2010), IIAS (2011–2013), and Sydney (2014–2015).

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, and under Johannes Schmidt, Otto Jahn, and Moriz Haupt. He was a professor at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

Ulrike Roesler works in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of Münster, she taught at Marburg and Freiburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her master's at Banaras Hindu University and her doctorate at the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti (~1975–1981). She was an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. His career was based at the Oriental Institute, Baroda, where he became deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam, and held posts at the FRLHT (1995), Amala Institute, and the University of Toyama (1998, 2003–2004).

Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University, under Junjiro Takakusu, and in Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He taught at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1930), Shukyo University, and Taisho University (~1926–1937).
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Koyasan in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juze-kai (1884), Kairitsu Gakko, and Jūzen hōkutsu.

Uranchimeg Borjigd Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and served as a research associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and UC Berkeley (PhD ~2003–2009), later holding posts at Berkeley, National University of Mongolia, Yonsei, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Urs App works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at Temple University (PhD) and Kyoto University under Seizan Yanagida and Yoshitaka Iriya. He served as professor at Hanazono University and associate director at IRIZ (1989–1999).

Usha Nilsson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She spent her career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she was a faculty member (attested 2001) and later Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia (attested 2026).
Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg (attested 2026).

Ute Hüsken specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Heinz Bechert (~1988–1995), teaching there until 2003 before holding professorships at the University of Oslo (2007–2017) and Heidelberg University (2017).

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at the University of Vienna starting in 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as a supervisor and guide (attested 2026).

V. P. Bhatta is a scholar of Indology and linguistics based at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he has headed the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and served as Professor-Editor (attested 2026).
V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who pursued PhD research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught at Madras (1934–1968), founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was its secretary (~1944–1979).
